A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same N-gram perplexity threat-model research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original HarmBench jailbreak experiments, filter ablations, transfer results, and a human evaluation of 2,000 responses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports additional multilingual filter evaluations, self-perplexity comparisons, and expanded transfer experiments.

M1.justification: The central bigram filter and most attack adaptations remain unchanged. However, Algorithm 2 changes adaptive PRS candidate generation to sampling the 100,000 most likely bigrams, and Appendix I introduces a PRS adaptation using self-perplexity as its rejection criterion. These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: v2 adds filter-rejection evaluation on translations of the 300 HarmBench queries into 12 languages, substantially extending the previously English-focused evaluation population (Section 5.3 and Table 2). The existing Dolma, Alpaca, and HarmBench coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated windowed and full-query self-perplexity comparators; the full-query result explicitly transfers the windowed attack (Table 3). BEAST and PAIR also enter comparisons on six retained target models where v1 reported no results. The preliminary COLD evaluation reported in v1 is removed.

E3.justification: Appendix F changes the reported PRS budget from 10,000 to 100,000 steps and its stopping condition from target probability above 0.1 plus a refusal check to probability above 0.99, followed by checkpoint judging. New self-perplexity experiments use separate stopping settings. The target-model configuration also changes: Zephyr-7b-R2D2 is removed, and transfer evaluation adds three large open-source models.

E4.justification: v2 adds multilingual utility tests and adaptive self-perplexity comparisons, and expands transfer analysis with additional targets and source-model ASR references. Figure 5 revises the threshold-sensitivity study and removes the separate GCG ASR-versus-FLOPs panel. The human evaluation and N-gram order/window ablations are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 5 explicitly reports average ASR and standard deviation over three seeds, with uncertainty bands. v1's corresponding figure provides neither a seed count nor uncertainty reporting; the PDFs establish newly reported uncertainty, not a known increase from a specified earlier run count.

E6.justification: PRS results are extensively replaced: baseline/adaptive ASR on Llama3.1-8b changes from 0.16/0.28 in v1 Table 4 to 0.97/0.96 in v2 Table 1, alongside the revised search procedure and budget. Perplexity distributions and transfer results also change, and new multilingual and self-perplexity entries are reported. Table 3 reports ASR 0.62 for all three filtered PRS conditions.

T1.justification: The formal threat-model definition changes: v1 Section 3.3 requires FLOPs below a fixed budget of 10^19, whereas v2 Section 3.4 treats FLOPs as a reported resource measure rather than a membership condition. The judge-success requirement remains in Equation 1, and the N-gram and adaptive-GCG mathematics are otherwise equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion recast the contribution from a joint perplexity/FLOPs-constrained threat model to an N-gram perplexity constraint with separate compute reporting. v2 additionally argues for N-gram perplexity over self-perplexity. The central claims about interpretable benchmarking and the strength of discrete-optimization attacks remain.

C2.justification: v2 drops v1's interpretation that filtering can improve PRS success and revises the model-robustness conclusions. Transfer is reinterpreted relative to declining source-model ASR, rather than simply as an absolute decline under tighter constraints. New discussions address multilingual and tokenizer limitations, Gemma's refusals after the target token, and whether self-perplexity confounds attack cost with robustness.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit HarmBench judge templates, judge precision, PRS reimplementation/caching information, and self-perplexity thresholds and context-handling details in Appendices B, F, G, and I. The main code-repository link remains, while the standalone reproducibility statement and separate baseline-repository links disappear. These extend and revise existing documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations concerning circuit breakers and latent-space defenses, multilingual tokenization, N-gram modeling, and layered safety measures. It also develops the comparison with earlier self-perplexity filters. The principal positioning around HarmBench and adaptive jailbreak evaluation remains intact.

P1.justification: Beyond retitling and widespread prose editing, v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative and experimental sections. Human evaluation moves from Appendix B to Section 5.6, filter-construction material moves into Appendix C, and related work and interpretation receive newly separated subsections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout, with extensive figure and table relocation and redesigned algorithms. v2 adds multilingual and self-perplexity tables and Figure 14, removes v1's attack-metric overview table, redraws transfer displays, and adds uncertainty bands to the PRS threshold plot.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens scrutiny of the central threat model: it documents a more thorough PRS search, fills previously missing attack comparisons, and directly tests adaptive self-perplexity alternatives. Multilingual tests and three-seed uncertainty reporting expose important applicability and variability limits. Conflicting calibration descriptions in Table 3 versus Appendix I and some mismatched captions weaken reporting, but the more complete and diagnostic evaluation provides a substantial net improvement.
